description: β numerical validation — Monte Carlo check of the analytical variance formula for the octonion associator, Fano-triple case. Setup (per docs/research/variance_of_associator.md § "Worked example:
comments: β numerical validation — Monte Carlo check of the analytical variance
formula for the octonion associator, Fano-triple case.
Setup (per docs/research/variance_of_associator.md § "Worked example:
single Fano generator"):
A(a, b, c) := ‖[a, b, c]‖²   where [a,b,c] = (a·b)·c − a·(b·c)
Unperturbed: [a,b,c] = 2·e_7, A = 4.
Perturb a_1 → 1 + δ, δ ~ N(0, σ²). The analytical first-order GUM
variance (from the β document, derivation):
Var(A) ≈ 64 σ²                                (TRUTH)
If the current compiler's stepwise scalar-product rule were applied
instead, it would give:
Var_compiler(A) ≈ 16 σ²                       (COMPILER, 4× low)
This test computes the sample variance of A over N = 100,000 Monte
Carlo samples and compares to the TRUTH formula. It does NOT test the
compiler's variance_of() — that requires the full Knowledge<f64>
chain which introduces unrelated complexities (see ζ buffer bug). The
compiler comparison is deferred to a separate test.
Pass criterion: |MC_var − 64σ²| / 64σ² < 0.05 (5% relative error).
If this passes, β's analytical formula is validated empirically. The
remaining claim — that the compiler produces 16σ² — is then a
separate reading-confirmation task.

comments: DISSERTATION 1-STATE QSS ANALYTICAL REFERENCE — RAPAMYCIN
Closed-form quasi-steady-state limit of PBPK28 at (V_v → 0, PS → ∞):
V_eff · dC_b/dt = -cl_hep · C_b + release
V_eff = V_b + Σ V_i · Kp_i
C_b(0+) = M_0 / V_eff (instantaneous redistribution)
C_b(t) = C_b(0+) · exp(-cl_hep · t / V_eff)
C_avg_i(t) = Kp_i · C_b(t)   [i ≥ 1];  C_avg_0(t) = C_b(t)
Consumed by scripts/ci/dissertation_pbpk28_parity_gate.sh Case 2 — the gate
compares the PBPK28 fully-coupled-CN degenerate trajectory against this
analytical limit and reports the convergence residual as the Type B
model-form uncertainty contribution per JCGM 100:2008 §4.3.
CORRECTED MATH (commits c574ee81 + this commit):
PBPK28 at (V_v→0, PS→∞) does NOT reduce to PBPK14. It reduces to *this*
1-state QSS model. PBPK14 well-stirred is the *intermediate* model where
within-organ redistribution is instantaneous but Q-transport between
blood and tissue remains rate-limited. The hierarchy is
PBPK28-literature → PBPK14 → 1-state QSS
with monotonically decreasing model-form complexity. Discrepancies
between successive tiers are Type B uncertainty contributions.

instruction: Write a Sounio run-pass example named `knowledge_layout_shadows_user_field_name`. A user struct field named `value` was silently clobbered by its sibling. `ir_register_knowledge_layout` preseeds a synthetic `Knowledge` layout — value@0, variance@1, confidence@2 — as entry 0 of the struct layout table,. It should compile and run successfully. Expected stdout: oid=85,29 value=170,187 variance=7 confidence=9
description: A user struct field named `value` was silently clobbered by its sibling. `ir_register_knowledge_layout` preseeds a synthetic `Knowledge` layout — value@0, variance@1, confidence@2 — as entry 0 of the struct layout table,
comments: A user struct field named `value` was silently clobbered by its sibling.
`ir_register_knowledge_layout` preseeds a synthetic `Knowledge` layout —
value@0, variance@1, confidence@2 — as entry 0 of the struct layout table,
before any user struct is registered. `field_idx_from_name_simple` resolves a
field *name* to a slot by scanning the whole table in order and taking the
first hit in any struct, and that path is what runs whenever the base is not
a typed local: `arr[i].f` reaches it because array locals record a length but
no element type.
So `ext[0].value` resolved to Knowledge's slot 0 — the same slot as `oid` —
and `ext[0].value = val_buf` overwrote the `oid` written just before it. Both
reads then went to slot 0 too, so `value` read back correct while `oid`
returned `value`'s bytes: a silent wrong answer at rc=0, with no diagnostic.
The trigger was the identifier, not the shape. The same program with the
field named `val` was always correct, at any struct size, array length or
index form — which is why size- and index-threshold hypotheses all died.
Guard all three preseeded names. Anything reading its sibling's data here
means the synthetic layout is shadowing user layouts again.
Honest scope: CI runs this suite under souc-stage2, which never carried the
defect, so this file is green either way there — it is the readable witness,
not the guard. The discriminating gate is the `knowledge_field_shadow` case
in tests/madaros/source_to_elf/manifest.tsv, which compiles with Madaros and
was measured red before this fix and green after.

comments: N2 negative control (codex ruling 2026-08-23, round 3 -- grok-4.6's
env-φ finding): `var x = measure(1); if c { x = measure(2) }; use(x)`
must NOT let x's post-if type revert to measure(1)'s narrow set. The bug
was structural, not just "wrong branch wins": checker_check_block_inplace
push_scope()s/pop_scope()s around every block including if-arms, and
pop_scope discards ANY env rebind made inside -- so the reassignment
literally never reached anywhere outside the branch, AS IF it had not
happened. checker_merge_ns_reassigned_inplace (called at the if/match
merge point) closes this: reassigning a Knowledge var while
ns_branch_depth > 0 records the name instead of a rebind that would just
be discarded, and the merge re-binds it in the NOW-RESTORED outer scope
with noise_set_id forced to top.
The observable proof is NOT just the "env_join" trace line at the merge
(that only proves the merge RAN) -- it's reading x again afterward: `x +
w3` unions x's POST-merge type with an empty set, so its own "union=-1"
line is the end-to-end proof that the forced-top value actually survived
past the if-statement into the code that follows it.
Per-rule sabotage: SOUNIO_NS_SABOTAGE_JOIN=1 disables the env-merge
(same knob as the CFG-join fixes), reproducing the pre-fix bug: x reverts
to its PRE-if handle, and the trailing union's handle becomes a real
(non-top) combination of that stale handle with w3's empty set instead
of -1 -- proving the env-join, not something else, closed the hole.
